answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, switching primary vendors now carries unacceptable delivery risk despite memory_c2's cost-cutting appeal—onboarding risk under a hard deadline is too high. Memory_c4 shows that renegotiating with the incumbent at renewal, backed by market benchmarking, recovered real margin and improved terms without disrupting supply continuity, which memory_c1 corroborates as stable across cycles. This path directly addresses the 18% spend-cut mandate while preserving delivery continuity. I verified memory_c4 and memory_c2 to confirm the negotiation outcome was durable and to weigh the switching option's actual risk profile before ruling it out this cycle. I flag downstream risk because memory_c6 warns that volume-based cost cuts can sometimes narrow service scope even when unit price improves, so the negotiated terms must be checked for scope erosion, not just price. Second-sourcing (memory_c3) remains attractive for the constrained-component risk but is deferred since only one action fits this cycle and the expiring contract is more time-critical. Confidence is moderate because verification will show whether the same benchmarking leverage applies to this specific vendor and category today.
